title: Cognitive psychology
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn how the mind processes information, and how psychologists find out: attention, perception and pattern recognition, working memory, long-term memory and forgetting, categories and concepts, mental imagery, problem solving and reasoning, judgment and decision making, and metacognition, with the classic experiments, the reaction-time and accuracy methods behind them, and the debates about how to interpret them.

weeks.1: Cognition and its methods: reaction time, accuracy and the information-processing view
weeks.5: Long-term memory: encoding, storage and retrieval
weeks.6: Forgetting, false memory and eyewitness testimony

blocks.deliverable: Analyze supplied reaction times from a cueing experiment.
Estimate a memory span and a search slope from supplied data.
Fit a forgetting curve to supplied recall data.
Week 7 midterm; compare prototype and exemplar accounts on supplied data.
Design a short decision experiment and predict its results.
Critique a classic experiment and propose a better test.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Replication study: choose one classic finding (such as the Stroop effect, the testing effect or visual search), run a small online or in-person replication with friends who consent, analyze the reaction times or accuracies with the methods of the course, and write a lab report that compares your result with the original and discusses what differs.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
